newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares close down as market tracks Dow.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares close down as market tracks Dow.

text.p: Brazilian shares took a hit on Thursday in the first session of the new year as Wall Street lost ground amid renewed fears of accelerating inflation, brokers said.
"Without local news to look to, the market here basically tracked the Dow," one trader said.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most-traded stocks ended down 1.2 percent at 69,555 points.
The bolsa's volume was 253.8 million reais ($244.2 million) of shares in another holiday-thinned session. The markets were closed Tuesday and Wednesday to mark the new year.

Analysts said share prices could rebound somewhat on Friday on hopes that the government will decide to exempt stock trades from a new financial transaction tax that will take effect later this month.
Brazil's top economic policy-makers will meet tomorrow to discuss the issue, though an official announcement of the government's decision may not be made until next week.

Market watchers hope that at least foreign investors in the bolsa will be exempt from paying the so-called CPMF tax, which would levy a 0.2 percent charge on all financial transactions to fund the country's health service.
Benchmark Telebras preferred ended off 1.88 percent at 78.50 reais, while the company's common stock fell 0.54 percent to close at 74.10 reais.
State mining concern Companhia Vale do Rio Doce dropped 2.5 percent to 19.50 reais, while state oil company Petrobras preferred lost 0.91 percent, ending at 164 reais.

Sao Paulo bourse's power-sector index, comprising the nine most liquid stocks of the electrical sector, fell 0.26 percent to 1,935 points, despite a rise of 1.04 percent in federal power utility Eletrobras.
Cemig shares fell 3.93 percent to 34.01 reais.
On the first trading day of the new year, the Sao Paulo bourse introduced a 100-share index. The so-called IBX, or Brazil Index, fell 0.78 percent to 1,528 points, the bolsa said.
The index will only be updated once a day at the end of trading and include the bolsa's most representative shares on the basis of trade and volatility.
